subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should upgrades handle existing trigger-script cron jobs whose creator-derived tool cap was never recorded and cannot be reconstructed?
rationale: The implementation cannot distinguish legitimate unrestricted operator jobs from jobs created through restricted agents, so preserving, warning on, or disabling those jobs is a security-versus-compatibility choice that requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Land Forward Protection
options.body: Merge the proven forward fix now and add prominent operator-facing audit guidance or diagnostics for existing cap-less trigger jobs.

options.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
options.body: Block cap-less legacy trigger evaluation until an operator reviews and re-saves each job with an explicit tool policy.

options.title: Pause for Provenance Design
options.body: Hold the PR while designing a broader persisted provenance mechanism that can classify legacy trigger jobs without stopping them all.

recommendation.title: Land Forward Protection
recommendation.body: Merge the proven forward fix now and add prominent operator-facing audit guidance or diagnostics for existing cap-less trigger jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent tool-authorization and cron-runtime history most directly spans both sides of this security and compatibility decision.
